title: The bash 5 floor is checked only in the dispatcher's process, so a handler exec'd through a PATH that finds bash 3.2 runs on it without refusal
body:
The bash >= 5 floor (issue 0022) is checked in exactly one process: `bin/devbin`, at its line 22, against the bash running the dispatcher. Handlers are separate processes. `exec_handler` in `lib/resolve` runs each one by `exec "$handler"`, so a handler gets whatever `#!/usr/bin/env bash` resolves on PATH, and nothing checks that bash again.

**Measured on 2026-09-16 at 16:36Z, through the dispatcher.** vc ran a throwaway clone of devbin at `5653ec7`, never this tree, with one project handler added that prints `$BASH_VERSION`:

    $ bin/devbin probe
    handler bash: 5.3.15(1)-release (/opt/homebrew/bin/bash)

    $ env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin /opt/homebrew/bin/bash bin/devbin probe
    handler bash: 3.2.57(1)-release (/bin/bash)
    rc=0

The dispatcher passed its own floor check on bash 5.3 and then ran the handler on macOS's 3.2 with no refusal. The same happens whenever a handler is run directly rather than through `bin/devbin`. The suite already does that: `tests/unit/infra-check.bats`, "a missing resolver is ONE error naming the tool", runs `$INFRA` under `env -i PATH=<links to /usr/bin and /bin>`.

**The reach is narrow.** With an ordinary PATH, `env bash` finds the same bash 5 for the dispatcher and for the handler. It takes a dispatcher started by an explicit bash while PATH resolves `bash` to 3.2, or a handler run directly. That can happen in cron, in `env -i`, in a CI step or a hook with a minimal PATH, or when someone types a full path to bash.

**Why it matters now.** 0060 was ruled option A on 2026-09-16: `shopt -s inherit_errexit` in `lib/helpers`, guarded by bash version. cc's measurement found this case, because the unguarded line died at load on 3.2 in the test above. The guard keeps a 3.2 handler working. It also keeps such a handler exposed to 0060 and to every other bash-5 assumption in the runtime, and nothing says so. A handler on 3.2 is outside the floor devbin declares, and today it runs silently.

**Fix shape, not ruled.** The floor check could also live where every handler passes through, which is `lib/helpers` -- the same file 0060's line goes into. It would refuse with the dispatcher's message instead of running. If that lands, 0060's version guard has nothing left to guard, and the unguarded form would be safe. So the two should be sequenced together. The same pre-notice reservation applies, because `lib/helpers` is vendored.


---

## Fixed 2026-09-16 -- landed with 0060 (vc), reviewed by dc

**Commits:** `acddd4d` (the fix) and `a58fb1d` (the two arms dc's review asked for).

`bash_floor_refuse` is the one refusal. It sits at the top of `lib/helpers`, ahead of the load guard, and must stay parseable by 3.2. Every process that sources `lib/helpers` refuses on its own interpreter: the dispatcher (which lost its own copy of the check and now sources `lib/helpers` as soon as the runtime is found) and every built-in handler.

`require_path_bash_floor` also asks the bash that PATH resolves, because that is the one every `#!/usr/bin/env bash` handler runs on. It refuses below 5, naming the path, and refuses a bash that cannot answer or answers something other than a number. When the PATH bash is the running `$BASH`, it costs one lookup.

This issue's own measured case (`env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin <bash 5> bin/devbin probe`) is an arm against the real `/bin/bash`.

**The finding it surfaced:** `tests/unit/infra-check.bats`'s no-dig link farm had been running its handler on 3.2 all along. It now links the suite's bash.

**Arms:**

- a PATH stub answering 3;
- a stub that cannot answer;
- a stub answering a non-number;
- a different PATH bash at >= 5 still runs (the over-refusal control);
- the measured case against the real 3.2;
- `lib/helpers` refusing to load on the real 3.2.

**Mutation checks:** vc's six were all killed. dc's review killed R1 (the refusal prints but does not exit); R2 (no non-numeric check) and R3 (could-not-ask passes) survived until the two arms at `a58fb1d`. The suite is 1150/1150 at `acddd4d`, where the real-3.2 arms ran and did not skip.

**Residuals, agreed with dc:**

- On Linux, the in-process floor is armed only by tests that skip there, so macOS CI carries it.
- A project handler that sources nothing from devbin is covered when dispatched, not when run directly. `intent/llm/ARCHITECTURE-shell.md` says so.
